items.title: Trading from free YouTube: take 5 strategy videos (3 Quantified Strategies, 2 Kevin Davey), write each one's rules from the transcript, rebuild the backtest on free daily data, then run neurotrader's permutation test (github neurotrader888/mcpt) to see which survive beyond luck; report published figure vs mine vs permutation p-value
items.note: Quantified Strategies numbers replicate when rules are given: RSI(5) triple 93 trades vs their 90, RSI(2)<9 235 vs 233 at PF 2.62 vs 2.59 (exit unstated, recovered as close above yesterday high); one video withheld its rules for members. Luck test (neurotrader permutation, 1000 shuffles): RSI(5) p 0.001 since 1993 and 0.03 to 0.04 since 2009; RSI(2) passes before 2009, fails after (p 0.21); 200 vs 222-day filter fails (p 0.057, best-of-281 0.18) and every length made less than holding SPY (14x vs 32x). Davey golden cross and RSI crossover on 12 daily ETFs: 1 and 0 of 12 markets under p 0.05, matching his pass and meh verdicts. Next: paper-track RSI(5) on SPY forward.

items.title: Paper-track SPY RSI(5) simple and triple forward, the only survivors of P-0082: each night after the US close compute the signal from Yahoo daily bars and commit it before the next open, log fills at the close as the rules say, score win rate and average trade against the backtest after 20 trades
items.note: Built the systems book (systems/): RSI(5) dip-buying on nine index ETFs fixed in advance, both fills, append-only signals, pass marks before the first trade (KILL under zero mean at 30, KEEP at 60 with t 1.65), wired into preregister, killcheck and the live nightly. Basket backtest 2009-26: 970 trades, about 55 a year, +0.64% a trade at the next open, 75% winners, every market positive, Japan weakest. First close (6 Oct): no signals. The replay against the backtest caught a trade-count bug in P-0082, now corrected; p-values unchanged.

items.title: Trend following the way the funds run it: one portfolio across 20+ markets (index, bond, gold, oil, currency and commodity ETFs), volatility-sized positions, a 100 to 250 day breakout or moving-average signal, scored against holding a 60/40 portfolio and with the permutation test on the whole portfolio, not one market at a time
items.note: Trend following as one 28-ETF portfolio, volatility-sized, parameters committed before the run, 2008-2026: 12-month momentum 3.2% a year (Sharpe 0.28, drawdown 35%), 100-day breakout 4.1% (0.33, 40%), against 60/40 at 8.7% (0.79, 31%). Luck test p 0.15 and 0.086: not cleared. Its use is as a hedge: correlation -0.11 to 60/40, +19% in 2022 when 60/40 lost 16%, and half-and-half halves the 60/40 drawdown to 15% for about two points a year less return. Not added to the systems book.

items.title: Dip-buying family on SPY and the nine-ETF basket: Williams %R(7) below -95, slow stochastic (7,3) below 25, IBS, SPY down 5% in 5 days, three lower closes; each luck-tested, plus the share of trade days each has in common with the RSI(5) book, to see whether these are separate edges or one trade (TRADING-IDEAS.md A-03 A-04 A-16 A-22 A-24)
items.note: Quantified Strategies replicates again, 5 for 5 (Williams %R(7) 289 trades vs their 288, PF 2.63 vs 2.61; stochastic 394 vs 394). The family is mostly one edge: with the 200-day filter 75 to 97% of trades overlap RSI(5), and unfiltered they average 0.27 to 0.34% on the basket against RSI(5) 0.64%. Down-5%-in-5-days and three-lower-closes fail the luck test even on SPY since 1993. The exception is IBS below 0.2: 23% overlap, p under 0.05 in all four US markets, and its trades with no RSI(5) trade open average +0.51% (3,395) against -0.49% inside one; real-time version queued as P-0091.

items.title: Darvas box breakout on SPY (12-day high, 0.75% chase cap, volume filter): replicate Quantified Strategies' 279 trades and profit factor 3.08, then the permutation test and the nine-ETF basket (TRADING-IDEAS.md A-01)
items.note: Trade count replicates (277 to 282 v their 279) but profit factor does not (2.34 to 2.61 v 3.08; first era 1.7 v 2.7) and their 12-day-best sweep does not reproduce (16 days best here). Luck test passes on SPY (p 0.011 full, 0.014 from 2009, volume permuted with the bars) yet random entries with the same exit earn a median +0.25 pct a trade against the real +0.28, so the exit is the edge. Nine ETFs from 2009: SPY alone passes, pooled +0.11 pct, 1 of 9 under p 0.05. Not a book candidate.

items.title: Calendar events on daily SPY since 1993: Fed decision days and the pre-Fed drift (dates from the Fed's own calendar pages), jobs-report Fridays, and the weak-Monday reversal (Monday closes below Friday's low, hold to Friday), each against random days of the same length (TRADING-IDEAS.md C-05 C-06 A-05)
items.note: Fed statement days 2016-26 (85 scheduled, dates from the Fed's pages) show nothing on daily bars: decision day +0.03 pct, the day before +0.09, three-day run-in +0.16, all level with other days (bootstrap p 0.4 to 0.6). Jobs Fridays (first Friday, 405 since 1993) average +0.15 pct against -0.05 for other Fridays, p 0.000. Weak Monday (close below Friday's low, hold to Friday close, 355 cases) +0.71 pct a trade, 66 pct winners, against +0.15 for any Monday, p 0.000; since 2009 +0.69. Claim of 0.6 reconciles. Not separated from a generic down-day dip; queued.

items.title: Kaufman efficiency ratio (net change over total path) on the 28 P-0084 ETFs: rank which markets trend, then test whether trading only the trendiest half, chosen on past data only, beats all 28 under the joint permutation test (TRADING-IDEAS.md B-01 B-11)
items.note: One-year efficiency ratio ranks HYG, QQQ, SPY, LQD top and FXI, FXC, EWZ, TLT bottom (all about 0.05 to 0.10). Trading only the trailing-two-year trendiest 14 of 28 with P-0084's momentum rule: Sharpe 0.23 against 0.35 for all 28 and 0.36 for the least trendy 14; top minus bottom -0.13 with p 0.77 under the joint shuffle (500). Smoothness last year does not predict momentum profit next year. Side finding: the all-28 baseline re-runs at 0.35, not P-0084's recorded 0.28, on the same data files; unexplained, re-read P-0084 before quoting it.

items.title: Stricter luck test for the systems book's RSI(5) basket: walk-forward permutation (neurotrader888 mcpt walkforward script) and a same-trade random-entry control with 10,000 draws, reported beside the in-sample p-values from P-0083 (TRADING-IDEAS.md frameworks)

Monthly timing models: replicate Antonacci global equities momentum (SPY vs EFA vs AGG, 12-month returns against T-bills) and the Fabian 39-week three-index model, luck-test both and score against 60/40 (TRADING-IDEAS.md A-13 A-12)

IBS as a second systems book, real-time rule: IBS below 0.2 at the close, buy the next open, sell the next open after a close above yesterday's high, taken only when the RSI(5) book is flat at that close; nine-ETF basket 2009 on, luck-tested per market and pooled, beside RSI(5) alone and the two combined (from P-0085)
items.note: Passes its pre-registered mark, narrowly: IBS below 0.2 taken only while the RSI(5) book is flat, nine ETFs 2009-26, 3,943 trades (about 220 a year), +0.27% a trade before costs, 65% winners, pooled luck test p 0.044, positive in all nine. A US effect: SPY, DIA, IWM pass alone, the overseas five do not. P-0085 hindsight +0.51% did not survive; gated equals ungated. With book 1 the pair has Sharpe 0.77, half SPY drawdown, under half its return. Added as systems book 2, judged after 0.05% costs, KILL at 200 if negative, verdict at 500.
